story: Dot matrix printer playing “Eye of the Tiger” [video]
text: A loudspeaker is nothing but a coil, a magnet and a piece of cardboard and it too is capable of incredible tonal quality and a huge range of polyphonics. This one really got me: [VIDEO]

I love this demo. It’s a good example of how much our perception is affected by our priors. This is a other great example, where speech is synthesized with an acoustic piano (though the keys are controlled digitally, the sound is just from the hammers and strings). Without the subtitles you probably couldn’t understand, but it sounds pretty clear when you know what it’s saying already. [VIDEO]

story: Auditory illusions with examples from Daft Punk
text: It's the Shepard tone effect running in the background of the actual notes, which produce a mild illusion that they're ascending when they're not, but nevertheless they're moving up and then down in pitches so it's not a brilliant example. I think the author is a little confused in this short essay about a few things. His "talking piano" effect is just standard vocoding, which has made me think this is all fairly new to him and he's not an expert. THIS is a talking piano: [VIDEO]

story: Computer program writing great, original works of classical music
text: talk about complex to play: [VIDEO] eerie! You're correct about the 'reproducing pianos', I didn't know the correct English term.
